learnerMaterial.title: Find the Constant of Proportionality
learnerMaterial.subject: mathematics
learnerMaterial.lessonGoal: Today you will find the constant of proportionality in tables and equations, then explain what it means in context.
successCriteria: I can test whether y/x stays constant.
I can interpret k with units.
keyPoints: In a proportional relationship, y/x has one constant value k.
The equation y = kx represents the relationship.
The constant has meaning and units in a context.

vocabulary.definition: the fixed multiplier k in y = kx

sections.title: Look for one multiplier
sections.body: A bike rental charges the same amount per hour. Divide cost by hours in each row.

sections.title: Worked example: connect table and equation
sections.directions: The solution is complete on this page. No response is expected.

items.prompt: What is the constant of proportionality for the bike rental, and what does it mean?

steps: Compute y/x for more than one row: 14/2 = 7 and 21/3 = 7.
In this situation, 7 means the rental costs $7 per hour.

sections.title: Your turn: find k
sections.directions: Use one row, then check with another.

items.prompt: A machine fills 18 bottles in 3 minutes and 30 bottles in 5 minutes. What is k in bottles per minute?

feedback.correct: Both rows give the same bottles-per-minute rate, so your k is supported by the table.
feedback.incorrect: Divide bottles by minutes for each row. A proportional table should give the same quotient twice.

items.prompt: Which equation matches a proportional relationship with k = 2.5?

feedback.correct: You placed k as the multiplier in y = kx.
feedback.incorrect: Use the proportional form y = kx. Decide where 2.5 belongs in that structure.

items.prompt: The equation d = 4.5t gives distance d in miles after t hours. Explain what 4.5 means and include units.

feedback.correct: You interpreted k as a unit rate instead of repeating the number without meaning.
feedback.incorrect: Read d/t: distance divided by time. State what amount of distance occurs for one hour.

sections.title: Reteach: use the one-row test
sections.body: For a pair (x, y), ask: “What multiplies x to make y?” That multiplier is a candidate for k. Check it on a second pair.

items.prompt: For the pairs (4, 10) and (8, 20), what is k?

feedback.correct: Your multiplier works for both ordered pairs.
feedback.incorrect: Solve 4k = 10, then check whether the same k makes 8k = 20.

items.prompt: A table contains (3, 12), (7, 28), and (10, 40). Decide whether it is proportional. Give k, an equation, and evidence from the table.

feedback.correct: Your ratios, equation, and conclusion support one another.
feedback.incorrect: Compute y/x for all three pairs. If they agree, use that common value in y = kx.

whatYouLearned: A proportional relationship has a constant ratio y/x.
The equation y = kx names the constant as k.
A useful interpretation of k includes units and context.
